title: Mortgage Broker Pipeline
description: For mortgage brokers: loan files by stage, rate locks, conditions, closings and partners.

spec.useCase: Concetta Ruiz processes loan files for a small mortgage brokerage and uses this to see which files close this month, which conditions are still open, which locks end soon and which referral partners to call. Tracking only; it holds no rates or financial advice.

text.text: The pipeline of a mortgage brokerage: every borrower and loan file from pre-approval to funding, the rate lock and closing date on each, the underwriting conditions still open, and the agents and partners who send you business.

This workspace is the brokerage's pipeline: every borrower, every loan file by stage, the rate lock and closing date that cannot be missed, the conditions the underwriter still wants, and the partners who refer you. Your loan origination system stays the place where applications and disclosures are produced; this is where the team sees the whole pipeline at once.

text.text: The Tanaka construction loan's appraisal came in low and the lock ends this week. The loan officer asks for a reconsideration of value with three better sales and, in parallel, prices a lock extension so the borrower can decide the same day.
Borrower files hold income, credit and bank information. Keep the documents themselves in your secure loan system and keep notes here to what the team needs to move the file.
Every loan moves through the same stages. Each stage has an entry test, so the pipeline report means the same thing to everyone.

text.text: Some conditions can only be met close to closing, such as a final verbal check of employment or an updated statement. Mark them
funding so they are not chased too early, and put a reminder on the closing countdown.
Conditions waiting on the borrower for more than two days get a phone call, not another email. The daily view of conditions due this week drives the processor's calls.
Abara's title commitment is past its date and closing is this week. The processor calls the title company, learns it is waiting on a payoff figure, and gets the payoff the same morning.
The last ten days before closing are where loans fail. A fixed countdown, checked every morning, keeps closings on their date.

text.text: Ask every new agent you work with on a deal for a ten-minute coffee after closing. Show them how your updates work. Agents who saw one smooth closing are the easiest new partners to win.

Desmond, the attorney at Keystone Title Counsel, was due a call three days ago and has a purchase in process. The loan officer calls with an update on the file and asks about two clients of his who mentioned refinancing.
When a file has a problem, call the partner before the borrower's closing is at risk, with what happened and the plan. Partners forgive problems; they do not forgive surprises.
Never pay or give anything of value for referrals. Shared marketing must follow the rules for your state and loan types; when in doubt, ask your compliance contact.
